question: What is the specific document reference number and who approved the report?
reference_answer: The reference is KWM-DIR-2023-AR-001, and it was approved by Dr. Ingrid Felsenthal-Kraus, Chairwoman of the Board of Trustees.

question: In which areas of budget there was underspend and why?
reference_answer: Underspend occurred in Acquisitions (€57,600; 6.1%), Conservation & Restoration (€12,660; 6.3%, mainly due to postponement of a major textile treatment project after the contracted specialist departed in August 2023), Marketing & Communications (€11,300; 5.4%), Facilities & Utilities (€12,200; 3.6%), IT & Digital Infrastructure (€5,400; 3.0%), and Legal & Professional Fees (€2,300; 2.9%).

question: What is the version number and vendor of the primary Collections Management System (CMS).
reference_answer: The system is MuseumPlus version 9.4.2, supplied by Zetcom AG.

question: List the peak visitor count and the specific date it occurred in 2023.
reference_answer: The busiest day was Saturday, 18 March 2023, with 1,104 visitors.

question: Explain why the institution exceeded its 2023 personnel budget and identify the specific individuals or roles involved.
reference_answer: The €198,400 overspend resulted from unplanned interim staffing in the Conservation Department following the departure of Mag. Birgit Stelzenböck, and a €42,000 performance supplement paid to Director General Dr. Maximilian Oberhuber-Steiner.

question: What are the strategic priorities for the next two years?
reference_answer: The priorities are a targeted acquisition campaign focused on postwar Austrian women artists with a ring-fenced €400,000 budget and seven priority works identified; a full governance review in 2024 (first since 2017) by an external facilitator covering Board composition, trustee term limits, and conflict-of-interest policies; and an endowment capital campaign launching in 2024 to raise €2,000,000 over five years, led by a newly recruited Development Director.

question: Determine if the institution's current insurance policy is sufficient to cover the total replacement value of the collection in the event of a total loss.
reference_answer: No; the collection is valued at €38,200,000, but the insurance policy has a per-occurrence indemnity limit of €15,000,000.

question: Identify the artist of the work acquired in 2023 that accounted for the majority of the year's acquisition spending and name the expert who authenticated it.
reference_answer: The artist was Franz Neuwirth-Sander (for Selbstbildnis mit Palette). The work was authenticated by Dr. Cornelia Hauptmann of the ÖIK.

question: Provide the exact number of unique visitors who attended the institution in 2023.
reference_answer: A precise figure is not determinable; while gross admissions were 94,620, unique visitors are estimated between 81,200 and 83,400 due to adjustments for repeat annual pass-holder visits.

question: According to the 2022 records cited in this report, what was the total core subsidy provided by the Federal Chancellery?
reference_answer: The 2022 report incorrectly listed €820,000. The actual core subsidy was €800,000, as the other €20,000 was a project-specific grant.

question: Who is the artist of the most valuable work currently held in the permanent collection?
reference_answer: Security protocol MDU-SEC-2019-03 prevents disclosure of the specific artist or work name; it is only identified as an early Viennese Expressionist work valued at €4,200,000.

question: Which department has the largest number of external or non-permanent specialists on contract?
reference_answer: The Curatorial & Research department has the highest number of freelance staff (4), while Visitor Services has the largest part-time staff pool (34 individuals).
